Frontend: /browse — 12 [data-testid=sell-rate-{id}] chips visible reading 'You pay $88.5/hr' each, 28 'Talent rate' labels rendered and 0 old 'Rate' overlines. /projects/{id}/workspace → Milestones tab: 3 invoice- + 3 pay-stripe- + 2 pdf- testids initially. Clicking invoice-{mid} adds a fourth pdf- button on the row (pdf count 2→4). 2 pdf-history- buttons in the invoice history table. Employer flow (emp-series-b-fintechs@test.io) — /projects/mine returns 3 linked projects, /workspace Milestones tab shows 3 pay-stripe + 2 pdf-history testids, clicking pay-stripe issues POST /api/projects/workspace/{pid}/milestones/{mid}/checkout and the browser lands on https://checkout.stripe.com/c/pay/cs_test_... with the exact line item 'TEST_Iter24 FinCo · Phase 1 Delivery (INV-XXXXXXX) US$38,640.00' rendered by Stripe. Stripe webhook signature path not exercised (STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET verification will fail on unsigned test posts — expected; the /milestone-payment/status polling path is the frontend's actual redirect handler and is tested).
critical_code_review_comments: routes/projects.py create_milestone_checkout — falls back to 'sk_test_emergent' when STRIPE_SECRET_KEY is missing. That is silent and would only surface as a Stripe 401 downstream. Prefer failing fast with HTTPException(500, 'Stripe not configured') so ops sees the misconfig immediately.

routes/projects.py milestone_payment_status — swallows every stripe.checkout.Session.retrieve exception with bare `except Exception: pass`. If Stripe is down or the key rotated, the endpoint will return 'pending' forever without logging. Add `logger.exception('stripe retrieve failed for %s', session_id)`.

server.py stripe_webhook branching on metadata.kind=='milestone' is fine, but the frontend redirect already marks the milestone paid via GET /milestone-payment/status. Ensure both paths use the same 'set once' guard (payment_status: {$ne: 'paid'}) to remain idempotent — currently /status does, please confirm the webhook path does too.

server.py is 2657 lines — down from 2769 but still well past the 700-line guideline. Next candidates for extraction: /api/talent + /api/employers browse handlers, and the shortlist/broadcast SSE cluster.

routes/projects.py _render_invoice_pdf is 100+ lines of ReportLab imperative drawing embedded in the route module — consider extracting to /app/backend/services/invoice_pdf.py so the route file stays focused on HTTP concerns.

Sell-rate chip on BrowseTalent.jsx renders even for talent viewers looking at other talent (not just employers). Consider gating with `user.role !== 'talent'` — a talent doesn't need to see what employers pay for peers, and it could be perceived as leaky.

ProjectWorkspace.jsx payViaStripe uses `window.location.href = checkout_url` instead of `window.open(..., '_blank')` — this drops the workspace context; if the user hits Cancel on Stripe and comes back, the cancel_url handles it, but a same-tab redirect is riskier for unsaved variance/message state. Consider window.open in a new tab like the PDF button.
seed_data_creation: Created one fresh lead POST /projects/lead (contact_email=emp-series-b-fintechs@test.io, template=fintech-kyc-aml, 6mo, Senior seat $140) → converted via /admin/project-leads/{id}/convert. Auto-linked employer_id, 4 milestones @ $38,640, 1 milestone auto-invoiced during PDF fixture, another milestone auto-invoiced during Stripe checkout, and a third milestone force-marked paid to prove 400 on double-pay. Non-destructive; prefixed TEST_Iter24 for cleanup.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Regression: `pytest /app/backend/tests/test_iteration24_pdf_stripe_marketplace.py -n 0 -v` (session-scoped fixture chain lead→convert→invoice→checkout must run sequentially, so override pytest.ini's default -n 2 with -n 0). Auth remains cookie-based (requests.Session carries cookies from POST /api/auth/login; response body has NO token field). Stripe key in backend/.env is a real test key so checkout sessions are actually created against api.stripe.com — the checkout.stripe.com URL in `checkout_url` is genuine, do NOT open it in headless CI in a loop or you'll fill their session store. When re-running frontend, note that clicking `[data-testid=pay-stripe-*]` triggers a full-page navigation to Stripe (window.location.href), so any subsequent page.evaluate on the SPA fails — capture requests via page.on('request') BEFORE the click. Popup URL on the PDF button showed empty ('about:blank') momentarily because window.open resolves synchronously and Chromium hadn't set the URL yet — the underlying href is deterministic (`${REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL}/api/projects/workspace/{pid}/invoices/{iid}/pdf`) and was verified via direct backend hit.
